glossary.TSH: Thyroid-stimulating hormone, released by the pituitary to drive the thyroid; low when the thyroid is overactive on its own.
glossary.Free T4: The unbound, active form of thyroxine in the blood, measured in thyroid function tests.
glossary.T3: Triiodothyronine, the most active thyroid hormone, mostly made by converting T4 in the tissues.
glossary.T4: Thyroxine, the main hormone made by the thyroid gland.
glossary.Thyroid function tests: Blood tests of TSH and free T4 (sometimes T3) used to diagnose thyroid over- or underactivity.
glossary.TFTs: Thyroid function tests: TSH and free T4, sometimes T3.
glossary.Basal metabolic rate: The energy the body uses at rest to keep its organs working.
glossary.Metabolic rate: How fast the body uses energy; thyroid hormone sets it.
glossary.Sympathetic overactivity: Too much 'fight or flight' nervous activity: fast heart, sweating, tremor, anxiety.
glossary.Heat intolerance: Feeling uncomfortably hot in conditions others find normal.
glossary.Fine tremor: A small, fast shake, best seen in the outstretched hands.
glossary.Palpitations: An unpleasant awareness of your own heartbeat.
glossary.Tachycardia: A heart rate over 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Menstrual irregularity: Periods that are unpredictable, lighter or missed.
glossary.Ophthalmopathy: Disease of the eye and orbit; in Graves' the eye muscles and fat swell and push the eyes forward.
glossary.Autonomously functioning nodule: A thyroid lump that makes hormone on its own, ignoring TSH.
glossary.Hashimoto's disease: Autoimmune thyroiditis that usually causes hypothyroidism, sometimes after a brief overactive phase.
glossary.Thyroiditis: Inflammation of the thyroid gland, which can leak stored hormone into the blood.
glossary.Post-viral: Coming on after a viral infection.
glossary.Isotope uptake: How much of a radioactive tracer the thyroid takes up on a scan, showing how active it is.
glossary.Thyroid uptake scan: A nuclear scan after a radioactive iodine or technetium tracer that shows which parts of the thyroid are active.
glossary.Delirium: An acute, fluctuating confusion with poor attention, caused by physical illness.
glossary.Osteoporosis: Thin, weak bones that fracture easily.
glossary.Hoarseness: A rough or weak voice, here a warning of recurrent laryngeal nerve damage.
glossary.Anterior neck mass: A lump in the front of the neck, often thyroid.
glossary.Pituitary MRI: An MRI scan of the pituitary gland, looking for a tumour.
glossary.Neutropenia: A low neutrophil count, which raises the risk of serious infection.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.Adrenergic symptoms: Symptoms from adrenaline-like activity: tremor, palpitations, sweating, anxiety.
glossary.Antithyroid drug: A drug such as carbimazole or PTU that blocks thyroid hormone production.
glossary.Definitive treatment: Treatment that removes the cause for good, such as radioiodine or surgery.
glossary.Compressive goitre: A goitre big enough to press on the windpipe or gullet.
glossary.Relapse: Return of the disease after treatment has controlled it.
glossary.First trimester: Weeks 1 to 12 of pregnancy, when the baby's organs form.
glossary.NSAIDs: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs such as ibuprofen.
glossary.Corticosteroids: Steroid drugs such as prednisolone or hydrocortisone that reduce inflammation; in thyroid storm they block T4-to-T3 conversion.
glossary.Antiarrhythmics: Drugs that control abnormal heart rhythms.
glossary.Fluid resuscitation: Giving IV fluids quickly to restore circulating volume.
glossary.Lithium: A mood stabiliser that also blocks thyroid hormone release; second-line in thyroid storm.
glossary.IV: Intravenous: given straight into a vein.
glossary.Beta-blocker: A drug that blocks adrenaline's effect on beta-receptors, slowing the heart.
glossary.IgG: The main antibody class in the blood; Graves' antibodies are IgG.
glossary.Hyperplasia: Growth of a tissue by an increase in cell numbers.
glossary.Pituitary feedback: The loop where high thyroid hormone tells the pituitary to make less TSH.
glossary.Autoregulatory shutdown: The thyroid switching off hormone production when faced with a large iodine load.
glossary.Iodine: The element the thyroid needs to make T3 and T4.
glossary.Cardiac output: The volume of blood the heart pumps each minute.
glossary.Catecholamines: Adrenaline-type chemicals that drive the fight-or-flight response.
glossary.Decompensation: When the body's compensating mechanisms fail and organs start to fail.
glossary.Hypothyroidism: An underactive thyroid with too little thyroid hormone.
